# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 82 (Bu-Vb Pc82)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc82  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 82  
**Title (English, from literature):** Diverting gains intended for the Sangha  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pariṇāmana-sikkhāpada* is the eighty-second rule in the Pācittiya section of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga. The rule establishes that a monk incurs an offense requiring confession if he knowingly diverts to an individual an offering or gain (*lābha*) that had been dedicated to the monastic community (*saṅgha*) [Dutt 1924; Stache-Rosen 1984]. Sukumar Dutt notes that this rule legally precluded individual appropriation of Saṅgha-dedicated property, restricting monastic members strictly to usufruct rights rather than individual ownership [Dutt 1924]. Ute Hüsken similarly highlights that Pācittiya 82, together with Nissaggiya Pācittiya 30, strictly regulates and prohibits the diversion of goods destined for the community to an individual [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
